summary:
Plateau State is a North Central state in Nigeria with its capital at Jos and a population of around 4.7 million. It stands under Nigeria's national criminal framework, principally the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014, which criminalises same-sex conduct, bans same-sex cohabitation and public shows of same-sex affection, and carries penalties of 10 to 14 years' imprisonment. Shari'a criminal law does not apply in Plateau, so the death-penalty exposure that applies in Nigeria's twelve northern states does not apply here; criminal liability rests on national statutory law alone.

No arrests, prosecutions, venue closures or recorded incidents of violence against trans or gender-nonconforming people specific to Plateau appear in the sources surveyed. No Plateau police action, court proceeding or state government statement on trans or gender-nonconforming people is documented in this record. The most recent documented incident of trans-specific violence in the sources is the killing of a transgender woman in Abuja in August 2024, which remained unprosecuted six months later; no later instance is documented.

A 2022 legal challenge resulted in a court ruling that Sections 4(1), 5(2) and 5(3) of the 2013 Act are unconstitutional and unenforceable in any part of the country, including Plateau. The sources report no legal protections for LGBTQ+ people in Nigeria and frequent violence against them, and Plateau is not recorded as having the concentration of arrests and communal tension attributed to the North Central zone.

National patterns that a trans visitor in Plateau would still face include police extortion and arbitrary arrest on the basis of gender presentation, 'kito' gang luring through dating applications leading to beating, filming and blackmail under threat of outing, and reluctance among LGBTQ+ people to seek medical care or report crimes to police for fear of arrest and extortion. Proposals to criminalise cross-dressing have been reported nationally and were met with fear among transgender Nigerians (Reuters, September 2022).
tangentialFactors:
Plateau's position in Nigeria's North Central zone places it outside the Shari'a-affected northern states, so the death-penalty risk identified in UK travel advice for northern Nigeria does not apply here; the applicable exposure is the national statutory penalty of up to 14 years' imprisonment.

The sources do not record the concentration of arrests and communal tension attributed to the North Central zone as being present in Plateau specifically. Mass arrests at private gatherings and hotels documented elsewhere in Nigeria (Asaba, Delta State, June 2018; Egbeda, Lagos, August 2018; Warri, Delta State, August 2023; Gombe State, October 2023) have no recorded Plateau equivalent in this record.

outOfScopeNotes:
